name: Joshua Tree Camping
tagline: For campers and backpackers visiting Joshua Tree National Park, where you bring every drop of water yourself.
description: Covers a 2-4 night cool-season trip (October-May) for a small group at a park campground or in a backcountry zone on a Recreation.gov backpacking permit. Assumes no water inside the park except at Black Rock and Cottonwood campgrounds, big day-night temperature swings and little or no cell service. Summer visitors should plan around extreme heat; backpackers can drop the campground-only items.
considerations: Black Rock, Cottonwood, Indian Cove, Jumbo Rocks, Ryan and Sheep Pass campgrounds are reservation-only up to 6 months ahead; Hidden Valley, White Tank and Belle are first-come and are usually full by Friday afternoon from October to May (NPS, as of 2026).
Only Black Rock and Cottonwood campgrounds have water. The park recommends at least 1 gallon per person per day and more when hiking in heat; keep extra water in the vehicle.

Backcountry camping requires a $6 Recreation.gov permit (1-12 people, up to 14 nights) in one of 15 zones, at least 1 mile from a trailhead, half a mile from roads and 200 ft from trails. Campfires are illegal in the backcountry.

Campground fires are allowed only in the provided rings with wood brought from outside the park; a seasonal campfire ban has run from about June 15 to October 1 in recent years. Check current fire restrictions.
Temperatures top 85 F from April to September; hike before 10 am or after 4 pm in heat. Flash floods can occur even on sunny days during summer monsoon season.
Cell service is extremely limited; download offline maps and the NPS app and share your itinerary. Search and rescue can take hours or days to reach you.
Campsite limits: 6 people, 3 tents and usually 2 vehicles; generators only 7-9 am, noon-2 pm and 5-7 pm; first-come sites must be paid within an hour.

sources.title: Safety Guidelines for Your Visit to Joshua Tree National Park

items.text: Campground reservation on Recreation.gov (up to 6 months ahead)
items.note: Or a first-come plan for Hidden Valley, White Tank or Belle with an early arrival.

items.text: Backcountry permit if backpacking ($6, 1-12 people, up to 14 nights)
items.note: Book on Recreation.gov up to 6 months ahead; choose one of 15 zones (as of 2026).

items.text: Check current fire restrictions and the heat or storm forecast
Itinerary shared with someone at home (no cell service)
Offline maps and the NPS app downloaded before arrival
Firewood bought outside the park (no gathering)
Cash or card for first-come site fees
At least 1 gallon of water per person per day; 2 gallons in heat
items.note: Only Black Rock and Cottonwood campgrounds have water.

items.text: Extra water left in the vehicle for emergencies
Bottles or bladder for 3 liters on hikes
Tent with sturdy stakes for wind and rocky ground
Sleeping bag warm enough for near-freezing nights
items.note: Fall, winter and spring nights get cold even after hot days.

items.text: Warm layers and beanie for cold nights

items.note: Fire bans are common; a stove is the reliable option.

items.text: Food in sealed containers or the vehicle (ravens, rodents, coyotes)
Comb and tweezers for cholla spines
Vehicle with full tank, good spare tire and extra water
Backcountry: WAG bags, or bury waste 200 ft from water (no water nearby anyway)
No fires in the backcountry; campground rings only
Stay on trails; do not climb or damage Joshua trees
Respect generator hours and quiet hours
